title: MADRA: Multi-Agent Debate for Risk-Aware Embodied Planning
abstract: arXiv:2511.21460v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit impressive reasoning capabilities but often suffer from "Embodied Semantic Hallucinations" - generating plans that are semantically fluent but physically unsafe due to a lack of grounded common sense. Existing safety alignment methods, such as RLHF or naive safety prompting, typically fall into a "Safety-Utility Trade-off," resulting in severe over-rejection of benign household instructions. To address this, we propose MADRA (Multi-Agent Debate for Risk Awareness), a training-free cognitive architecture that mimics System-2 deliberation. MADRA introduces a meta-cognitive Critical Agent that evaluates peer debates using a structured argumentation framework derived from the Toulmin Model, effectively mitigating the "herd mentality" in multi-agent systems. We also introduce SafeAware-VH, a benchmark featuring adversarial safe instructions designed to probe agents' sensitivity to physical risks. Exten

translated_title: MADRA：面向风险感知具身规划的多智能体辩论
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型展现出令人印象深刻的推理能力，但常常遭受“具身语义幻觉”的困扰——生成的计划在语义上流畅，但由于缺乏扎根于现实的常识而在物理上不安全。现有的安全对齐方法（如RLHF或朴素的安全提示）通常陷入“安全-效用权衡”，导致对良性家庭指令的严重过度拒绝。为解决这一问题，我们提出了MADRA（面向风险感知的多智能体辩论），一种无需训练、模拟系统2深思式推理的认知架构。MADRA引入了一个元认知的批判智能体，使用源自图尔敏模型的结构化论证框架来评估同伴辩论，有效缓解了多智能体系统中的“从众心理”。我们还推出了SafeAware-VH基准，其中包含对抗性安全指令，旨在探测智能体对物理风险的敏感性。
tldr: MADRA提出了一种无需训练的多智能体辩论认知架构，通过元认知批判智能体和基于图尔敏模型的结构化论证来缓解大语言模型的“具身语义幻觉”、避免安全-效用权衡，并发布了SafeAware-VH基准用于评估具身智能体的物理风险感知能力。
